summary: A TikTok video of three 11- and 12-year-old Swifties struggling to open a "1989 (Taylor's Version)" CD went viral, drawing over 2.7 million views and a comment from Taylor Swift herself. The girls had bought the CD to cheer up their friend Annika, who broke her wrist at soccer practice. The moms found the moment a reminder of how technology has changed since CDs, introduced in 1982, were largely replaced by digital music like iTunes.
one_line: Three young Taylor Swift fans went viral on TikTok struggling to open a 1989 (Taylor's Version) CD, and Swift commented "Wait, this is amazing."
key_facts: The video shows 11- and 12-year-olds Lilly, Henslee and Annika trying to open a "1989 (Taylor's Version)" CD.
The girls gave the CD to Annika to cheer her up after she broke her wrist during soccer practice.
Mom Shannon Schmidt said they had to borrow Grandma and Grandpa's CD player so the girls could fully experience the CD.
Lilly eventually released the CD from its case by pressing the middle of it.
The TikTok video has garnered over 2.7 million views and 5,952 comments.
Taylor Swift liked and commented on the video, writing "Wait, this is amazing."
Henslee said of Swift's comment: "That was the best surprise ever — my year is made."
A second video showed the girls figuring out the CD player, which was slightly easier; one said "This is a fancy one."
The overwhelming response from viewers was "I feel old."
In May, Fox News Digital reported on a mom whose 10-year-old daughter struggled to open a "Now That's What I Call Music! 21" CD (2006).
CDs were first introduced in 1982, according to Philips' website; Philips and Sony co-developed the technology.
Apple introduced iTunes in 2001, selling digital songs for 99 cents each, which has virtually replaced the CD in 2023.
